help.title: Help
help.intro: Here's a simple, jargon-free guide to getting the most out of Belrion.

customFields.title: Custom fields: adapt the app to your sector
customFields.intro: Belrion is used by salespeople across very different sectors — energy, hospitality, automotive and many more. A client's fixed data (company, contact, phone, email, address, notes, status) works for any sector, but your day-to-day probably needs to track something more specific. That's what custom fields are for: you create them, tailored to you, and decide who can see them.
customFields.step1Text: Go to Settings → Custom fields → press "Add field". Give it a name that's clear to you — it doesn't need to sound technical.
customFields.step1Example: Example: someone in the energy sector creates a field called "CUPS" to store each client's electricity supply code.
customFields.step2Title: 2. Choose the type and who can see it
customFields.step2Text: Every field has a type, based on what you'll store in it: Free text (for codes or short notes), Number, Date, Dropdown list (when the value is always one of a few you define), or Yes/No. You also choose whether the field is private (only you see and fill it in) or shared with your team (everyone on the team sees it and can fill it in on the clients you share).
customFields.step2Example: Example: someone in hospitality creates a Date field called "Last health inspection", and keeps it private since it's only for their own tracking.
customFields.step3Title: 3. Fill it in on each client's record
customFields.step3Text: Open any client's record and scroll down to the "Custom fields" section: every field you've created (yours plus anything your team shares) is there, ready to fill in.
customFields.step3Example: Example: someone in automotive opens a dealership's record and enters 45 in the "Vehicles in stock" field.
customFields.step4Title: 4. Show it as a column in the list
customFields.step4Text: In the client list, press the "Columns" button and check the custom fields you want to see at a glance in the table, without opening each record.
customFields.step5Text: With "+ Add filter" you can search clients by a custom field's value, just like you already do with status or product. And if it's shown as a column, you can click its header to sort the list by that field.

routeGenerator.title: Visit route generator: make the most of a free slot
routeGenerator.intro: Finished early, forgot to plan ahead, or just not sure who to visit today? The route generator suggests a list of clients in an area who are due for a revisit, so you don't have to comb through your portfolio by hand.
routeGenerator.step1Text: In Settings → Revisit cycle, set how many months should pass before you consider a client due for another visit. The generator only suggests clients who've gone longer than that cycle without a visit (or who have never been visited).
routeGenerator.step1Example: Example: with a 3-month cycle, a client you visited 2 months ago won't show up in the route yet; one you visited 4 months ago will.
routeGenerator.step2Text: Press "Generate visit route" in Calendar, type in a town or area (and pick your personal portfolio or a team's, if you belong to one), and the app will search for clients in that area whose address matches and who don't already have a pending visit scheduled. If none are found in the exact town, it automatically tries widening the search to its whole comarca — it will clearly tell you when that happened.
routeGenerator.step2Example: Example: you type "Granollers" and there are no pending-due clients in that exact town; the app widens the search to the Vallès Oriental comarca and suggests clients from nearby towns, clearly noting that the search was widened.
routeGenerator.step3Title: 3. Adjust the proposal and confirm it
routeGenerator.step3Text: On the review screen you can remove clients, reorder them with the arrows, and adjust each visit's time. Confirming creates them as normal visits in your Calendar — there's no new screen or table to check afterward, everything shows up where you already look.
routeGenerator.step3Example: Example: the app suggests 8 clients with times spaced 45 minutes apart starting at 9:00; you remove one because it's out of your way today, move up another's time, and confirm the route for today.
